summary: Your own words, cut up: {rival}'s side runs lines from {your writing}, cut from their context, every day.
realLife: Running for California governor in 1934, he was hit with out-of-context quotes from his own novels run daily in the papers, and with newsreels of staged voter interviews; studio heads pressured employees to give to his opponent. He lost.
gates: A body of writing or speeches on your record.
choices: say the words were a character's, not yours

branches.then: A big employer docks pay or presses staff to give to {rival}, and a worker tells you.
Filmed voter interviews against you turn out to use actors, and exposing it is a press story.
